Welcome—let’s take a moment together to think about what makes a house truly feel like home. Have you ever noticed how the little details, the way things are arranged, or the gentle order in your space, can completely shift your mood? That sense of sanctuary, the feeling that you really belong, so often starts right where you live.
In the book, Home Comforts: The Art and Science of Keeping House, Cheryl Mendelson invites us to see housekeeping in a whole new light. She explores the delicate balance between tradition and practicality, showing how even the tiniest rituals at home can turn an ordinary space into your personal haven. Suddenly, keeping house isn’t just another chore—it’s a comforting, meaningful practice that supports our health, happiness, and sense of belonging.
We’ll look at everything from the science behind dust and laundry, to the art of setting a table that says “welcome.” There’s real wisdom tucked into these routines—and a surprising joy that comes from caring for your space, one thoughtful choice at a time.
As we explore together, you’ll find stories and practical tips woven with cultural insights, all pointing to this one idea: when we take care of our homes, we’re really nurturing ourselves and those we love. So, get ready to discover that housework can be more than just work—it can be a way to create comfort, order, and a deep sense of well-being right where you are.
